analysis: The broad option combines programming, optimisation, decisions under uncertainty, machine learning, neural networks, reinforcement learning, numerical methods and robotics with psycholinguistics, perception, neurobiology and experimental cognition. Replacing general health psychology and persuasion makes the technical contribution more coherent.

The computational option emphasises databases, software, networks, advanced algorithms, learning and robotics. Software, algorithms and infrastructure distinguish it from the broad option’s cognition sequence. Both include a practical robotics course; the actual emphasis is kinematics and motion rather than a dedicated robot-learning lab.

The cognitive option focuses on language, perception, development, philosophy and human research. Programming, statistical learning, vision and neural networks supply computational methods. Replacing persuasion with data science strengthens the progression from data handling to model evaluation. Psycholinguistics is a substantive study of human language and cannot supply dedicated NLP. Dedicated MLOps and the formal graduation project remain gaps.

All 61 prior offering conflicts are resolved across the three current schedules. The provisional alignments use shared evidence wherever available and treat the public overview’s robotics course as a hypothesis pending the cohort decision. Options exceed the 30 EC pairwise floor. They remain provisional while stage 1 is unresolved.

alignment.rationale: Both provide a foundational introduction to programming for later computational study.
Both develop systematic software design and implementation practices.
Advanced Algorithms develops systematic computational problem solving; it is more algorithmically specialised than the UvA course.
Both use probabilistic models to reason under uncertainty. UCR covers Bayesian networks within a broader course on how agents make decisions.
Both directly cover data structures, algorithms and computational complexity.
Both use mathematical optimisation methods for computational and AI problems.
Both provide a dedicated introduction to machine-learning methods and model evaluation.
Both provide substantial neural-network theory and implementation, with UCR also extending into deep learning.
Both study robotics. UCR concentrates on kinematics, grasping and planning robot motion. The UvA overview describes a course on robots that learn.
Both directly cover image processing and computer-vision methods.
Both cover single-variable calculus, including differentiation, integration and mathematical problem solving.
Both develop linear-algebra foundations through matrices, vectors and transformations.
Both develop formal logic and discrete reasoning for computing and AI.
Both combine probability and statistical inference for data-driven modelling.
Both study aspects of language processing. UCR examines human language production, comprehension and acquisition. UvA builds computational language-processing methods.
Both ask philosophical questions about mind and intelligence. UvA also addresses ethics as part of its AI curriculum.
Both consider fairness, safety and societal impacts of AI. UCR also uses ethical theory and psychology to study human interaction with AI.
Both provide explicit first-year academic and professional formation; UCR PPD is broader than the AI-specific practicum.
